core_obligations: Show containment: if q is an associated prime of R modulo the n-th symbolic power of p then p is contained in q (proof lines 15784-15785).

Show that every x outside p is a nonzerodivisor on that quotient, using the description of the symbolic power as R intersected with p^n R_p: if xy lies in the symbolic power then y lies in p^n R_p and hence in the symbolic power (proof lines 15786-15790).
Combine the two halves to conclude that the only associated prime is p itself (proof line 15791).
proof_roadmap: Get p contained in every associated prime from the definition of the quotient (proof lines 15783-15785).
Test elements outside p for being nonzerodivisors using the localised description of the symbolic power (proof lines 15786-15790).
difficulty_reason: For a Noetherian ring R, a prime p and n greater than zero, the lemma states that the associated primes of R modulo the n-th symbolic power of p consist of p alone (statement lines 15776-15781). The proof does not use the theory of primary decomposition: it first gets p contained in every associated prime directly from the quotient, then shows that each x outside p is a nonzerodivisor on that quotient by writing the symbolic power as R intersected with p^n R_p and observing that xy in the symbolic power forces y into p^n R_p and hence back into the symbolic power (proof lines 15783-15792). The use of the localised description to run the divisibility test is the substance, and the author writes it out. H2.
